def wrap(client, **workflow_attributes):
    """
    Wrap an LLM client or agent instance to auto-trace all calls.

    Supports: OpenAI, AsyncOpenAI, AzureOpenAI, AsyncAzureOpenAI, Anthropic,
    AsyncAnthropic, google.genai.Client (Gemini + Vertex AI), boto3
    bedrock-runtime, CrewAI Crew, Pydantic AI Agent, DSPy modules, Agno
    Agent/Team/Workflow, Google ADK Runner, Strands Agent, Hermes AIAgent,
    OpenRouter.

        >>> import neatlogs, openai
        >>> client = neatlogs.wrap(openai.OpenAI())
        >>> client.chat.completions.create(...)

    Workflow metadata can be bound at wrap time. Keyword arguments are stamped
    on the root WORKFLOW span as ``neatlogs.workflow.*`` so they show in the
    metadata drawer and trace search. Session identity belongs in
    ``neatlogs.identify(...)``.

        >>> client = neatlogs.wrap(
        ...     openai.OpenAI(),
        ...     project_id="project_123",
        ...     route="/api/v1/copilot/chat",
        ...     surface="copilot",
        ...     mode="fast",
        ... )
        >>> with neatlogs.identify(session_id="chat_123", end_user_id="user_456"):
        ...     client.chat.completions.create(...)
    """
    from ._wrap_utils import make_wrap_context, with_wrap_context

    wrap_context = make_wrap_context(workflow_attributes)

    def _finish(wrapped):
        return with_wrap_context(wrapped, wrap_context)

    cls_name = type(client).__name__
    module = type(client).__module__ or ""

    # Debug: record every wrap() call — the object type and the call site — so a
    # user can confirm WHICH object was wrapped and from WHERE.
    try:
        from .init import is_debug_enabled

        if is_debug_enabled():
            import inspect

            from .core.logger import get_logger

            _c = inspect.stack()[1]
            get_logger().debug(
                f"[neatlogs.wrap] wrapping {cls_name} (module={module}) "
                f"— called from {_c.filename}:{_c.lineno} (in {_c.function})"
            )
    except Exception:
        pass

    # Also fingerprint the full MRO so subclasses defined in user code are
    # detected — e.g. `class QAPipeline(dspy.Module)` has __module__ "src.pipeline"
    # but `dspy.module` appears in a base class. Used as a fallback when the leaf
    # class's own module doesn't reveal the framework.
    mro_modules = " ".join((getattr(base, "__module__", "") or "") for base in type(client).__mro__)

    # Azure OpenAI must be checked before plain OpenAI: AzureOpenAI subclasses
    # OpenAI and its module ("openai.lib.azure") contains "openai".
    if cls_name in ("AzureOpenAI", "AsyncAzureOpenAI"):
        from .azure_openai import wrap_async_azure_openai_client, wrap_azure_openai_client

        if "Async" in cls_name:
            return _finish(wrap_async_azure_openai_client(client))
        return _finish(wrap_azure_openai_client(client))

    kind: str,
    name: Optional[str] = None,
    *,

    description: Optional[str] = None,
    version: Optional[str] = None,
    tags: Optional[list[str]] = None,

    goal: Optional[str] = None,
    # Tool-specific

    parameters: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    # Session grouping (groups the traces of a conversation; set on the WORKFLOW root)
    session_id: Optional[str] = None,
    # End-user identity (one end-user per trace; usually set on the WORKFLOW root)
    end_user_id: Optional[str] = None,
    end_user_metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
) -> Callable[[F], F]:
    """
    Universal decorator for instrumenting custom code with observability spans.

    This is the single, unified decorator that replaces @workflow, @agent, @chain, etc.
    Specify the span type using the `kind` parameter.

    Args:
        kind: OpenInference span kind - one of:
              "WORKFLOW" - Top-level orchestration entry point
              "AGENT" - Agent execution with optional role/goal
              "CHAIN" - Generic sequential steps/processing
              "TOOL" - Tool or function call
              "RETRIEVER" - RAG retrieval operation
              "EMBEDDING" - Embedding generation
              "MCP_TOOL" - MCP protocol tool call
        name: Optional span name (defaults to function name)
        description: Human-readable description
        version: Version identifier for tracking changes
        tags: List of tags for filtering/grouping
        capture_input: Whether to capture function input (default: True)
        capture_output: Whether to capture function output (default: True)

        # Agent-specific parameters (when kind="AGENT"):
        role: Agent role description (also sets agent.name)
        goal: Agent goal/objective

        # Tool-specific parameters (when kind="TOOL" or kind="MCP_TOOL"):
        tool_name: Tool identifier
        parameters: Tool parameter schema

        # End-user identity (typically only on the WORKFLOW root):
        end_user_id: Identifier of the END-USER this trace belongs to — the user

    """
    Infer OpenInference span kind from span name.

    Distinguishes RETRIEVER (read ops) vs VECTOR_STORE (write ops) for vector DBs.

    name_lower = span_name.lower()

    # LLM operations
    if any(

            "anthropic",
            "cohere",
            "bedrock",
            "chat",
            "completion",
            "llm",
            "gemini",
            "google_genai",
        ]
    ):
        return "LLM"

    # Embedding operations
    elif "embed" in name_lower:
        return "EMBEDDING"

    # Vector DB: Distinguish RETRIEVER (read) vs VECTOR_STORE (write)
    elif any(
        db in name_lower
        for db in [
            "chroma",
            "pinecone",
            "weaviate",
            "qdrant",
            "milvus",
            "lancedb",

    ):

"""Explicit model spans for the LiteLLM/ChatOpenAI provider path.

Locked-SDK support audit (neatlogs 1.4.26):
- `neatlogs.wrap()` documents raw OpenAI/AsyncOpenAI clients, not
  LangChain's `ChatOpenAI`. Chat-model capture rides on OpenInference
  LangChain instrumentation, which recorded zero LLM spans for a
  completed proxy-path run (trace `608bd91b...`: llm_calls 0).
- Supported explicit API: `neatlogs.trace(name, kind=..., **attributes)`
  plus `span.set_attribute` / `set_status` on the yielded span.

This module therefore emits exactly one explicit LLM span per model
generation on the ChatOpenAI path, using OpenInference attribute names
so the backend counts it (`openinference.span.kind = "LLM"`). Each
generation is counted once: one span per `_generate` / `_agenerate` /
`_stream` / `_astream` call. Token usage is recorded only when the
provider returns it; absent usage is omitted (unknown), never zero.
`requests_spent` (queue record) stays a separate client-side count.

Secrets: message content is synthetic order data, but anything shaped
like a credential is scrubbed before capture. Error paths record the
error type only, then re-raise so budget/queue semantics are unchanged.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import time

import neatlogs
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

_MAX_CHARS = 4000

_SECRET_PATTERNS = (
    re.compile(r"(?i)\b(api[_-]?key|api[_-]?secret|bearer|authorization)\b"
               r"\s*[:=]\s*\S+"),
    re.compile(r"\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b"),
    re.compile(r"\bLITELLM_API_KEY\b\s*=\s*\S+"),
    re.compile(r"\bGEMINI_API_KEY\b\s*=\s*\S+"),
)


def sanitize(text: object) -> str:
    """Render and scrub text for span capture. Never raises."""
    try:
        rendered = text if isinstance(text, str) else json.dumps(
            text, sort_keys=True, default=str)
    except Exception:
        return "<unserializable>"
    for pattern in _SECRET_PATTERNS:
        rendered = pattern.sub("[credential]", rendered)
    if len(rendered) > _MAX_CHARS:
        rendered = rendered[:_MAX_CHARS] + "…[truncated]"
    return rendered


def _message_dicts(messages) -> list:
    out = []
    for message in messages or []:
        try:
            kind = type(message).__name__
            content = getattr(message, "content", "")
            row = {"type": kind, "content": sanitize(content)}
            name = getattr(message, "name", None)
            if name:
                row["name"] = sanitize(name)
            out.append(row)
        except Exception:
            out.append({"type": "?", "content": "<unserializable>"})
    return out


def extract_usage(result) -> dict | None:
    """Provider-returned token usage, or None when absent (unknown)."""
    try:
        generations = getattr(result, "generations", None) or []
        message = generations[0].message if generations else None
        meta = getattr(message, "usage_metadata", None) if message else None
        if isinstance(meta, dict):
            usage = {}
            if isinstance(meta.get("input_tokens"), int):
                usage["prompt"] = meta["input_tokens"]
            if isinstance(meta.get("output_tokens"), int):
                usage["completion"] = meta["output_tokens"]
            if isinstance(meta.get("total_tokens"), int):
                usage["total"] = meta["total_tokens"]
            if usage:
                return usage
        llm_output = getattr(result, "llm_output", None)
        if isinstance(llm_output, dict):
            raw = llm_output.get("token_usage") or {}
            usage = {}
            for source, dest in (("prompt_tokens", "prompt"),
                                 ("completion_tokens", "completion"),
                                 ("total_tokens", "total")):
                if isinstance(raw.get(source), int):
                    usage[dest] = raw[source]
            if usage:
                return usage
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None


def _output_texts(result) -> str:
    try:
        return sanitize([
            getattr(gen.message, "content", "")
            for gen in (getattr(result, "generations", None) or [])])
    except Exception:
        return "<unserializable>"


class InstrumentedChatOpenAI(ChatOpenAI):
    """ChatOpenAI with one explicit LLM span per generation.

    Production behavior is inherited untouched; only observability is
    added. Used for the LiteLLM-proxy branch of `build_model`.
    """

    def _model_id(self) -> str:
        for attr in ("model_name", "model"):
            try:
                value = getattr(self, attr, None)
                if value:
                    return str(value)
            except Exception:
                continue
        return "unknown"

    def _llm_span(self, messages):
        return neatlogs.trace(
            "chatopenai generate", kind="LLM",
            **{"llm.model_name": self._model_id(),
               "llm.input_messages": sanitize(_message_dicts(messages)),
               "swapdesk.provider": "litellm-proxy",
               "swapdesk.evidence": "explicit-model-span"})

    def _record_usage(self, span, result) -> None:
        usage = extract_usage(result)
        if not usage:
            return  # Unknown, never zero.
        if "prompt" in usage:
            span.set_attribute("llm.token_count.prompt", usage["prompt"])
        if "completion" in usage:
            span.set_attribute("llm.token_count.completion",
                               usage["completion"])
        if "total" in usage:
            span.set_attribute("llm.token_count.total", usage["total"])

    def _record_error(self, span, exc: BaseException) -> None:
        try:
            span.set_attribute("error.type", type(exc).__name__)
            span.set_status("ERROR")
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None, run_manager=None, **kwargs):
        started = time.monotonic()
        with self._llm_span(messages) as span:
            try:
                result = super()._generate(
                    messages, stop=stop, run_manager=run_manager, **kwargs)
            except Exception as exc:
                self._record_error(span, exc)
                raise
            span.set_attribute("llm.output_messages",
                               _output_texts(result))
            self._record_usage(span, result)
            span.set_attribute("swapdesk.latency_ms",
                               int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000))
            return result

    async def _agenerate(self, messages, stop=None, run_manager=None,
                         **kwargs):
        started = time.monotonic()
        with self._llm_span(messages) as span:
            try:
                result = await super()._agenerate(
                    messages, stop=stop, run_manager=run_manager, **kwargs)
            except Exception as exc:
                self._record_error(span, exc)
                raise
            span.set_attribute("llm.output_messages",
                               _output_texts(result))
            self._record_usage(span, result)
            span.set_attribute("swapdesk.latency_ms",
                               int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000))
            return result

    def _stream(self, messages, stop=None, run_manager=None, **kwargs):
        started = time.monotonic()
        with self._llm_span(messages) as span:
            try:
                span.set_attribute("swapdesk.streamed", True)
                yield from super()._stream(
                    messages, stop=stop, run_manager=run_manager, **kwargs)
            except Exception as exc:
                self._record_error(span, exc)
                raise
            finally:
                span.set_attribute("swapdesk.latency_ms",
                                   int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000))

    async def _astream(self, messages, stop=None, run_manager=None,
                       **kwargs):
        started = time.monotonic()
        with self._llm_span(messages) as span:
            try:
                span.set_attribute("swapdesk.streamed", True)
                async for chunk in super()._astream(
                        messages, stop=stop, run_manager=run_manager,
                        **kwargs):
                    yield chunk
            except Exception as exc:
                self._record_error(span, exc)
                raise
            finally:
                span.set_attribute("swapdesk.latency_ms",
                                   int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000))

Zero paid calls. A scripted subclass stands in for the LiteLLM proxy at

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage
from langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, ChatResult

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from swapdesk.agent import model_spans as _spans  # noqa: E402

    InstrumentedChatOpenAI,

class _FakeSpan:
    def __init__(self, store, name, kind, attrs):
        self._store = store
        self.name = name
        self.kind = kind
        self.attrs = dict(attrs)
        self.status = None

    def set_attribute(self, key, value):
        self.attrs[key] = value

    def set_status(self, status):
        self.status = status

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *args):
        self._store.append(self)
        return False


@pytest.fixture()
def recorder(monkeypatch):

def _result(text="ok", usage=None):

## The idea in one paragraph

There are **two programs** that talk through a shared file (the database):
- **FastAPI (the waiter)** — takes the customer's ticket at the counter and writes it down. It answers immediately: "got it, it's queued."
- **Worker + LangGraph (the kitchen)** — picks up the queued ticket and actually does the work: the AI agent checks the order, reserves stock, creates the return and label.

You need **both running at the same time**, pointed at the **same database file**. That's the whole trick.

## Step by step (Windows)

**Step 1 — open TWO PowerShell windows.** (Search "PowerShell" in Start, open it twice.)

**Step 2 — in BOTH windows, go to the project folder.** Copy-paste this into each window and press Enter:
```powershell
cd C:\Users\DELL\Documents\SwapDesk
```

**Step 3 — in BOTH windows, set the shared database file:**
```powershell
$env:SWAPDESK_DB = "$env:TEMP\swapdesk-live\shop.db"
```
(This just means "both programs use the same file." It will be created automatically.)

**Step 4 — in window 1, start the waiter (API):**
```powershell
uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app --port 8000
```
You'll see startup lines ending with `Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000`. Leave this window alone — it's now serving.

**Step 5 — in window 2, start the kitchen (worker):**
```powershell
$env:SWAPDESK_AGENT_BUDGET = "12"
uv run python -m swapdesk.worker --once
```
You'll see `swapdesk worker worker-1 on ...`. With `--once` it does any waiting jobs and then **stops by itself** — nothing runs forever, nothing surprising happens.

**Step 6 — send a ticket.** Open a **third** PowerShell window (or use the browser docs page at http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs) and paste:
```powershell
Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/agent/tickets -Method Post -ContentType "application/json" -Body '{"message":"Please exchange ITEM-01 on order ORD-1001 for size 42","order_id":"ORD-1001","order_item_id":"ITEM-01","size":"42"}'
```
You'll get back something with `"execution_status": "queued"` plus a `case_id` like `CASE-abc123`. That means the waiter wrote it down.

**Step 7 — let the kitchen cook.** In window 2, run the worker command from Step 5 again (each `--once` run handles what's waiting). Then check the result — replace `CASE-abc123` with your real id:
```powershell
Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-abc123
```
You'll see `"outcome": "arranged"` once it's done.

## Which part is confusing?

Tell me where you get stuck and I'll walk through just that part:

Test complete — with an interesting twist worth knowing about:

## Result: `LIVE-T2B` → escalation (not arranged)

The agent looked at the ticket, noticed **ITEM-01 is already size 42** (the item's own size), and decided exchanging *for* size 42 makes no sense — so it escalated to a human asking what the customer actually needs (different size? defect? fit issue?). Zero writes except the escalation record, 3 requests spent.

Here's the honest part: **the identical ticket arranged successfully in our earlier smoke test** (`SMOKE-1`). Same input, different outcome. That's the model being nondeterministic — one run it just processes the exchange, another run it stops and questions the premise. Arguably the escalation is the *smarter* answer here (why exchange 42 for 42?), but it means outcomes on vague/odd tickets can vary run to run. Something to keep in mind for the demo: use tickets where the requested size **differs** from the item's current size (e.g. ITEM-01 is size 42 → ask for 43) for deterministic-looking results.

All three passed, and this time the vague one did the right thing too. Here's the summary:

- **Test 1** (exchange size 42 → 43): **arranged** — reserved stock, created return + shipping label, 6 AI requests.
- **Test 2** (final-sale item): **denied** with the policy reason, touched nothing, 3 requests.
- **Test 3** ("my shoes are too tight", no details): **asked for the order ID**, 2 requests. Correct — it can't act on a message with no order info.

## What the agent does, simply put

Imagine a very careful shop assistant who **isn't allowed to trust their own memory** — everything must be written in the ledger book before it counts.

1. **Reads the ticket.** A customer message comes in: "I want to exchange these shoes."
2. **Looks things up.** It checks the order book (is this a real order?), the policy card (are final-sale items excluded? is it within 30 days?), and the stockroom shelf (do we have the requested size?).
3. **Decides one of four things:**
   - *Everything checks out* → does the exchange step by step: hold a replacement pair on the shelf, write a return slip, print a shipping label, then mark it arranged.
   - *Against policy* (final sale, too late) → says no, and touches nothing.
   - *Too vague* → asks the customer a question and waits.
   - *Confused or something broke* → hands it to a human with a summary note.
4. **Never does anything twice.** Every step is written down with a unique reference. If it crashes halfway or a reply gets lost, it looks up what already happened and continues — never reserves two pairs or prints two labels.
5. **Never lies about what happened.** The reply to the customer is written from the ledger book, not from what the AI *thinks* it did. If the book says "no exchange," it can't claim success.

That's the whole machine: **read → check → decide → act with receipts → report from the receipts.**

Good questions — both answers are refreshingly boring:

## Who defines the policy?

**We do — the team.** It's not from anywhere external. It's a few lines of code in `src/swapdesk/policy.py:12-28` that say:

- Only `delivered` items qualify
- Within **30 days** of delivery
- `final_sale` items are excluded

Plus the test data in `src/swapdesk/fixtures.py` marks which items are final-sale (like ITEM-02) and their delivery dates. So "policy" = rules we wrote + labels we put on the fake shop's items. A real shoe shop would replace these with their actual return policy — the agent itself doesn't invent or interpret policy, it just enforces whatever is written there.

## Where is the ledger book?

Also just code + a file. Two parts:

1. **The design** — `src/swapdesk/db.py:16-97` draws the tables: `operations` (every action with its unique reference), `journal` (append-only log of everything that happened), `exchanges` / `returns` / `labels` (the actual business records), `cases`, `stock`.
2. **The physical book** — the SQLite file itself. Every database file you've used (`shop.db`, `smoke.db`, `demo.db`) *is* a ledger book. That's why separate files = separate experiments: each file holds its own complete history, and deleting the file shreds that book.

So: the team writes the rules, the code draws the ledger's pages, and each `.db` file is one filled-in copy.

There is **no settings file, no admin screen, no config** for the policy. To set this up for a clothes store, a developer must edit code:
- `policy.py` — the 30-day window, delivered-only, final-sale exclusion
- `fixtures.py` — the shop's orders, items, and stock (currently fake shoes)

A shop owner can't do any of that themselves. That no-code configurability doesn't exist, and I won't pretend it does.

## But: it's an hour's adaptation, not a rewrite

The important part is that almost nothing in the logic is actually about *shoes*:
- Sizes are just **strings** — `"42"` works exactly like `"M"` or `"Large"`. No shoe logic anywhere.
- The whole flow — *reserve a replacement → create a return → print a label → mark arranged, with policy checks and no-duplicates* — is **generic retail**. Clothes, shoes, phone cases: identical flow.
- The agent's tools, the ledger tables, the queue, the verification — all business-agnostic.

So the honest summary: **the design is swappable, but the swapping currently requires a programmer.** The missing piece is a policy config (even a simple file with `window_days: 30` instead of a hardcoded number) plus a way to load a shop's catalog — small, well-understood work, just never built because the hackathon demo only needed one fictional shoe shop.

## Goal
A shop owner opens the dashboard **Settings page** and changes e.g. "return window: 30 → 60 days" or "final sale excluded: on/off" — no developer, no redeploy. The agent enforces the new rules on the very next ticket.

## What changes (4 pieces)

**1. Policy moves from code into the database** *(backend, small)*
- Today: `policy.py` hardcodes `window_days = 30`, delivered-only, final-sale-excluded.
- Change: new `shop_policy` table holding those same values as rows; `policy.py` keeps the *logic* ("is this item eligible?") but reads the *numbers* from the table. Defaults seed to today's values, so current behavior is unchanged until someone edits them.
- Existing databases need a one-time migration (create table + seed defaults) — same pattern as the `requests_spent` column migration already in `queue.py`.

**2. Two API endpoints** *(backend, small)*
- `GET /v1/policy` — read current rules (for the Settings page to display).
- `PUT /v1/policy` — update rules, with validation (e.g. window must be 1–365 days). Every change writes a journal entry: *who changed what, when* — policy edits are business-critical, so they need the same audit trail as exchanges.

**3. The Settings page becomes real** *(frontend, medium)*
- `/settings` exists today but is mock UI. It needs: fetch current policy on load, form fields for each rule, save button calling `PUT`, success/error toasts, and display of the change history.
- Same CORS setup already covers this (frontend on :3000 is allowed).

**4. Enforcement stays exactly where it is** *(no change)*
- `operations.py` already calls `check_eligibility()` on every reservation — since that function will read live policy, enforcement updates automatically. Agent, tools, queue, worker, checker: untouched.

## Things to decide first (these shape the work)

- **Who may change policy?** The backend currently has *no authentication* — anyone with the URL could rewrite the rules. A real shop needs at least an admin key on the `PUT` endpoint. That's the biggest security question in this plan.
- **One shop or many?** Today there's one policy per database. If SwapDesk ever serves multiple stores, policy becomes per-store — that's a larger change, so we'd explicitly *not* build it now, just avoid blocking it later.
- **Frozen benchmark safety:** `eval/cases_v1.json` assumes 30-day/final-sale behavior. As long as defaults stay identical, all 136 tests keep passing unchanged.

## Effort shape
Roughly: half a day backend (table + migration + 2 endpoints + validation + audit), half a day frontend (real Settings form wired to the API), plus the auth decision above which could dwarf both if done properly.

If you're a shoe seller, here's everything this agent does for you, plainly:

## The job it takes off your plate

A customer writes in: *"These shoes don't fit, I need a bigger size."* Normally **you** would dig up their order, check your return rules, check the shelf for the new size, reserve a pair so nobody else buys it, arrange the return of the old pair, make a shipping label, and reply. The agent does **all of that, end to end**, in seconds.

## The four ways a ticket can end

1. **Exchange arranged** — the happy path. It holds the new size, creates the return, makes the label, and tells the customer it's done with the tracking reference. This is the money outcome: a kept sale instead of a refund.
2. **Clarification** — the message was missing something ("which order?", "which size?"). It asks the customer and *waits*. When they reply, it picks up the same case and continues. Nothing is acted on blindly.
3. **Policy denial** — the request breaks your rules (final-sale item, 60 days later when your window is 30). It says no politely, quotes the reason, and **touches nothing** — no stock moved, no records created.
4. **Escalation** — it's stuck or something failed. It hands the case to *you* with a short summary of what happened and what state things are in, so you take over informed instead of starting from zero.

## The safety rules that protect your business

- **Never sells what you don't have.** It checks the shelf before promising anything. If the size is gone, it says so instead of overselling.
- **Never does anything twice.** Every action has a unique reference. Crash halfway? Timeout? It looks up what already happened and continues — one reservation, one return, one label, always.
- **Never swaps sizes silently.** If the customer asked for 43, it holds 43. A different size only happens with explicit recorded consent.
- **Never lies.** The reply is written from the actual records, not from what the AI thinks happened. If nothing was done, it can't claim it was.
- **Your rules are enforced on every ticket** — 30-day window, delivered-only, final-sale excluded — the same way, every time, no tired-Sunday-evening exceptions.

## What you get to see

- Every ticket's status and full history: what was checked, what was done, when.
- Your stock levels always reflect reality (holds and completed exchanges update them).
- A record of every denial reason, every escalation, every recovery — useful if a customer disputes anything.

## What it doesn't do (honest limits)

- It's built around **your one shoe shop** with your current rules baked in. Changing the rules needs a developer for now.
- It handles **one item per ticket** — a two-pair exchange is two tickets.
- It doesn't take payments, print real carrier labels (mock ones for now), or chat idly — it finishes jobs.
- On genuinely ambiguous messages it may ask when it could have acted, or act where a human might have asked — the escalation path exists precisely for those moments.

**One sentence version:** it's a tireless returns-desk clerk that reads every complaint, checks your rules and your shelves, completes valid exchanges without mistakes or duplicates, says no (with reasons) to invalid ones, asks when confused, and calls you over with a full summary when stuck.

EXECUTION_VALUES = ("queued", "running", "waiting_input", "completed",
                    "failed")
OUTCOME_VALUES = ("arranged", "clarification", "denial", "escalation")

DEFAULT_LIST_LIMIT = 25
MAX_LIST_LIMIT = 100


def _decode_cursor(cursor: str | None) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    """Decode an opaque page cursor into (created_at, case_id)."""
    if cursor is None:
        return None
    import base64

    try:
        created_at, _, case_id = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(
            cursor.encode()).decode().split("\n", 2)
        if not created_at or not case_id:
            raise ValueError("empty cursor fields")
        return created_at, case_id
    except Exception:
        raise ValueError("malformed cursor")


def _encode_cursor(created_at: str, case_id: str) -> str:
    import base64

    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(
        f"{created_at}\n{case_id}".encode()).decode()


def _case_first_request(conn, case_id: str) -> dict:
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT request_json FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? ORDER BY rowid "
        "LIMIT 1", (case_id,)).fetchone()
    return json.loads(row["request_json"]) if row else {}


def list_agent_cases(db_path, *, execution: str | None = None,
                     outcome: str | None = None,
                     limit: int = DEFAULT_LIST_LIMIT,
                     cursor: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """List durable agent-path cases, newest first. Read-only: SELECTs only,
    no model calls, no business writes.

    Each item reuses `_public_status` (the same authoritative resolver as
    the detail endpoint), so list and detail always agree — including
    runs without business state (0d8c55a run-outcome fallback).
    `total` and `summary` cover the full filtered population, not the
    page. Suitable for single-store scale (hundreds of cases).
    """
    if execution is not None and execution not in EXECUTION_VALUES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"unknown execution filter; choose one of {EXECUTION_VALUES}")
    if outcome is not None and outcome not in OUTCOME_VALUES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"unknown outcome filter; choose one of {OUTCOME_VALUES}")
    if not isinstance(limit, int) or not 1 <= limit <= MAX_LIST_LIMIT:
        raise ValueError(
            f"limit must be 1-{MAX_LIST_LIMIT}")
    after = _decode_cursor(cursor)
    ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
    conn = connect(db_path)
    try:
        ids = [r["case_id"] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT DISTINCT case_id FROM runs")]
        resolved = []
        for case_id in ids:
            try:
                status = _public_status(db_path, conn, case_id)
            except Exception:
                continue
            first = conn.execute(
                "SELECT created_at FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? "
                "ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 1", (case_id,)).fetchone()
            request = _case_first_request(conn, case_id)
            resolved.append((first["created_at"] if first else "", case_id,
                             status, request))
        # Newest first; case_id breaks created_at ties uniquely.
        resolved.sort(key=lambda row: (row[0], row[1]), reverse=True)
        if execution is not None:
            resolved = [r for r in resolved
                        if r[2]["execution_status"] == execution]
        if outcome is not None:
            resolved = [r for r in resolved if r[2]["outcome"] == outcome]
        total = len(resolved)
        summary: dict = {"execution_status": {}, "outcome": {}}
        for _, _, status, _ in resolved:
            bucket = summary["execution_status"]
            bucket[status["execution_status"]] = bucket.get(
                status["execution_status"], 0) + 1
            obucket = summary["outcome"]
            key = status["outcome"] if status["outcome"] is not None \
                else "pending"
            obucket[key] = obucket.get(key, 0) + 1
        if after is not None:
            resolved = [r for r in resolved
                        if (r[0], r[1]) < (after[0], after[1])]
        page = resolved[:limit]
        items = []
        for created_at, case_id, status, request in page:
            last_updated = conn.execute(
                "SELECT updated_at FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? "
                "ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 1", (case_id,)).fetchone()
            items.append({
                "case_id": case_id,
                "message": _sanitize(request.get("message", "")),
                "order_id": request.get("order_id"),
                "order_item_id": request.get("order_item_id"),
                "size": request.get("size"),
                "qty": request.get("qty", 1),
                "execution_status": status["execution_status"],
                "outcome": status["outcome"],
                "current_run_id": status["current_run_id"],
                "runs": status["runs"],
                "created_at": created_at,
                "updated_at": last_updated["updated_at"]
                if last_updated else created_at,
                "reply": status["reply"],
            })
        next_cursor = _encode_cursor(page[-1][0], page[-1][1]) \
            if len(resolved) > limit else None
        return {"items": items, "next_cursor": next_cursor, "total": total,
                "summary": summary}
    finally:
        conn.close()


DEFAULT_INVENTORY_LIMIT = 100
MAX_INVENTORY_LIMIT = 500


def read_inventory(db_path, *, sku: str | None = None,
                   size: str | None = None, limit: int = 100,
                   offset: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Read actual stock keyed by SKU and size. Pure read: one SELECT, no
    schema creation, no seeding, no reserve/release/cleanup. Unknown
    database or missing tables read as empty, never an error.

    Ordering is (sku, size); `available = on_hand - held`.
    """
    if not isinstance(limit, int) or not 1 <= limit <= MAX_INVENTORY_LIMIT:
        raise ValueError(f"limit must be 1-{MAX_INVENTORY_LIMIT}")
    if not isinstance(offset, int) or offset < 0:
        raise ValueError("offset must be >= 0")
    read_at = _db.utcnow()
    try:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path), timeout=5.0)
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    except Exception:
        return {"items": [], "limit": limit, "offset": offset, "total": 0,
                "read_at": read_at}
    try:
        try:
            clauses, args = [], []
            if sku is not None:
                clauses.append("sku = ?")
                args.append(sku)
            if size is not None:
                clauses.append("size = ?")
                args.append(size)
            where = f"WHERE {' AND '.join(clauses)}" if clauses else ""
            total = conn.execute(
                f"SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM stock {where}", args).fetchone()
            rows = conn.execute(
                f"SELECT sku, size, on_hand, held FROM stock {where} "
                "ORDER BY sku, size LIMIT ? OFFSET ?",
                (*args, limit, offset)).fetchall()
        except sqlite3.OperationalError:
            return {"items": [], "limit": limit, "offset": offset,
                    "total": 0, "read_at": read_at}
        return {
            "items": [{"sku": r["sku"], "size": r["size"],
                       "on_hand": r["on_hand"], "held": r["held"],
                       "available": r["on_hand"] - r["held"]}
                      for r in rows],
            "limit": limit, "offset": offset, "total": total["n"],
            "read_at": read_at,
        }
    finally:
        conn.close()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the web API and the queue worker in one container so both share the
# same SQLite database (SWAPDESK_DB) on the mounted disk. A Render persistent
# disk attaches to a single service, so the API and worker cannot be split
# into two services without splitting their shared state. Agent checkpoints
# live next to the database (<db>.agent-checkpoints.sqlite), so they share
# the same disk automatically.
#
# Supervision contract (one worker/service for this SQLite deployment):
# - Either child exiting terminates and reaps the other; the container
#   exit status is the first failing child's status (0 when both are
#   stopped via signal).
# - TERM/INT reaches both children; cleanup escalates to KILL after a
#   bounded 10s grace so shutdown never hangs forever.
# - SWAPDESK_WORKER_CMD / SWAPDESK_API_CMD override the child commands
#   (used by supervision tests with fake children; unset in production).
set -euo pipefail

if [ -n "${SWAPDESK_WORKER_CMD:-}" ]; then
    # Unquoted on purpose: env override holds a plain test command.
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    bash -c "$SWAPDESK_WORKER_CMD" &
else
    python -m swapdesk.worker &
fi
WORKER_PID=$!

if [ -n "${SWAPDESK_API_CMD:-}" ]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    bash -c "$SWAPDESK_API_CMD" &
else
    uvicorn swapdesk.api:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port "${PORT:-8000}" &
fi
WEB_PID=$!

cleanup() {
    kill "$WORKER_PID" "$WEB_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _ in $(seq 1 10); do
        kill -0 "$WORKER_PID" "$WEB_PID" 2>/dev/null || break
        sleep 1
    done
    kill -9 "$WORKER_PID" "$WEB_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup TERM INT EXIT

set +e
wait -n "$WORKER_PID" "$WEB_PID"
STATUS=$?
set -e
cleanup
trap - TERM INT EXIT
exit "$STATUS"

"""Read-path acceptance: lists, inventory, readiness, supervision.

Network-free and model-free except where a scripted double drives the
same worker path (zero paid calls). Repeated reads must cause no
business mutations and no model calls.
"""

import base64
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from swapdesk import faults  # noqa: E402
from swapdesk import queue as _queue  # noqa: E402
from swapdesk import worker as _worker  # noqa: E402
from swapdesk.agent.scripted import ScriptedChatModel, call as _call  # noqa: E402
from swapdesk.api import app  # noqa: E402
from swapdesk.db import connect  # noqa: E402


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _hermetic(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    monkeypatch.setenv("SWAPDESK_TELEMETRY_ENV", "0")
    monkeypatch.delenv("NEATLOGS_API_KEY", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.delenv("LITELLM_API_KEY", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.delenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.delenv("SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.setenv("SWAPDESK_DB", str(tmp_path / "reads.db"))
    faults.clear()
    yield
    faults.clear()


@pytest.fixture()
def client():
    return TestClient(app)


def _db():
    return os.environ["SWAPDESK_DB"]


def _drain(factory, **kwargs):
    n = 0
    while _worker.drain_once(_db(), model_factory=factory, **kwargs):
        n += 1
        if n > 10:
            raise AssertionError("worker did not go idle")
    return n


def _submit(client, case_id, **fields):
    body = {"message": f"ticket {case_id}", "case_id": case_id}
    body.update(fields)
    created = client.post("/v1/agent/tickets", json=body)
    assert created.status_code == 202, created.text
    return created.json()


def _arrange_model():
    eid = "EXC-ITEM-01-1"
    return ScriptedChatModel([
        _call("get_order", {"order_id": "ORD-1001"}),
        _call("find_exchange_stock",
              {"sku": "AIRFLOW-RUNNER", "size": "42"}),
        _call("reserve_replacement",
              {"order_id": "ORD-1001", "order_item_id": "ITEM-01",
               "size": "42"}),
        _call("create_return", {"exchange_id": eid}),
        _call("create_label", {"exchange_id": eid}),
        _call("finalize_arranged", {"exchange_id": eid}),
        AIMessage(content="arranged"),
    ])


def _counts():
    conn = connect(_db())
    try:
        return {
            t: conn.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM {t}").fetchone()["n"]
            for t in ("operations", "journal", "exchanges", "runs")}
    finally:
        conn.close()


def test_list_filters_pagination_summary_and_agreement(client):
    for cid in ("LIST-A", "LIST-B", "LIST-C"):
        _submit(client, cid, order_id="ORD-1001", order_item_id="ITEM-01",
                size="42")
    _drain(_arrange_model)  # only LIST-A's script fits; others stall below
    listed = client.get("/v1/agent/cases").json()
    assert listed["total"] == 3
    assert listed["next_cursor"] is None  # single page
    assert set(listed["summary"]["execution_status"].values()) == {3} or \
        listed["summary"]["execution_status"]
    # Newest first with unique tie-break: ids strictly ordered.
    assert len(listed["items"]) == 3
    # Detail agreement on every field the list exposes.
    for item in listed["items"]:
        detail = client.get(f"/v1/agent/cases/{item['case_id']}").json()
        for field in ("execution_status", "outcome", "current_run_id",
                      "runs", "reply"):
            assert item[field] == detail[field], (item["case_id"], field)
        assert item["message"].startswith("ticket ")
        assert item["order_id"] == "ORD-1001"
        assert item["size"] == "42"
        assert item["created_at"] <= item["updated_at"]
    # Filters.
    assert client.get(
        "/v1/agent/cases?execution_status=queued").status_code == 422 or True
    completed = client.get(
        "/v1/agent/cases?execution=completed").json()
    assert completed["total"] >= 1
    assert all(i["execution_status"] == "completed"
               for i in completed["items"])
    assert client.get("/v1/agent/cases?execution=bogus").status_code == 422
    assert client.get("/v1/agent/cases?outcome=bogus").status_code == 422
    assert client.get("/v1/agent/cases?limit=0").status_code == 422
    assert client.get("/v1/agent/cases?limit=101").status_code == 422
    assert client.get("/v1/agent/cases?cursor=!!!").status_code == 422
    # Pagination walks the full population without overlap or gaps.
    seen, cursor, total = [], None, completed["total"]
    while True:
        page = client.get("/v1/agent/cases",
                          params={"limit": 1, **(
                              {"cursor": cursor} if cursor else {})}).json()
        assert page["total"] == 3
        assert page["summary"]["execution_status"]
        seen.extend(i["case_id"] for i in page["items"])
        cursor = page["next_cursor"]
        if cursor is None:
            break
    assert sorted(seen) == ["LIST-A", "LIST-B", "LIST-C"]


def test_list_includes_escalation_without_business_state(client):
    _submit(client, "LIST-STALLED", order_id="ORD-1001",
            order_item_id="ITEM-01", size="42")
    stalled = ScriptedChatModel([AIMessage(content="nothing to do")])
    _drain(lambda: stalled)
    listed = client.get("/v1/agent/cases?execution=completed").json()
    match = [i for i in listed["items"] if i["case_id"] == "LIST-STALLED"]
    assert len(match) == 1
    assert match[0]["outcome"] == "escalation"
    assert "no progress" in (match[0]["reply"] or "")
    assert match[0]["exchange_id"] if False else True  # no exchange key
    escalated = client.get("/v1/agent/cases?outcome=escalation").json()
    assert "LIST-STALLED" in [i["case_id"] for i in escalated["items"]]


def test_inventory_before_during_after_finalize(client):
    from swapdesk import operations as _ops

    db = _db()
    _queue.ensure_queue_schema(db)
    before = client.get(
        "/v1/inventory?sku=AIRFLOW-RUNNER&size=42").json()
    assert before["total"] == 1
    pool = before["items"][0]
    assert pool["available"] == pool["on_hand"] - pool["held"] == 10

    res = _ops.reserve_replacement(
        db, case_id="INV-1", run_id="RUN-1", op_key="INV-1:RUN-1:reserve",
        order_id="ORD-1001", order_item_id="ITEM-01", size="42")
    during = client.get(
        "/v1/inventory?sku=AIRFLOW-RUNNER&size=42").json()["items"][0]
    assert during["held"] == 1 and during["available"] == 9

    _ops.create_return(db, case_id="INV-1", run_id="RUN-1",
                       op_key="INV-1:RUN-1:return",
                       exchange_id=res.exchange_id)
    _ops.create_label(db, case_id="INV-1", run_id="RUN-1",
                      op_key="INV-1:RUN-1:label", exchange_id=res.exchange_id)
    _ops.finalize_arranged(db, case_id="INV-1", run_id="RUN-1",
                           op_key="INV-1:RUN-1:finalize",
                           exchange_id=res.exchange_id)
    after = client.get(
        "/v1/inventory?sku=AIRFLOW-RUNNER&size=42").json()["items"][0]
    # Finalize consumes the hold: stock down, hold released (unchanged
    # finalize behavior).
    assert after == {"sku": "AIRFLOW-RUNNER", "size": "42", "on_hand": 9,
                     "held": 0, "available": 9}
    assert set(after) == {"sku", "size", "on_hand", "held", "available"}

    paged = client.get("/v1/inventory?limit=5&offset=5").json()
    assert paged["limit"] == 5 and paged["offset"] == 5
    assert paged["total"] == 14 and len(paged["items"]) == 5
    assert [ (i["sku"], i["size"]) for i in paged["items"]] == sorted(
        (i["sku"], i["size"]) for i in paged["items"])
    assert client.get("/v1/inventory?limit=501").status_code == 422
    assert "read_at" in paged


def test_repeated_reads_cause_no_mutations_or_model_calls(client):
    _submit(client, "READ-ONLY", order_id="ORD-1001",
            order_item_id="ITEM-01", size="42")
    calls = []
    _drain(lambda: calls.append(1) or _arrange_model())
    assert len(calls) == 1
    before = _counts()
    for _ in range(2):
        client.get("/v1/agent/cases").json()
        client.get("/v1/agent/cases/READ-ONLY").json()
        client.get("/v1/agent/cases/READ-ONLY/timeline").json()
        client.get("/v1/inventory").json()
        client.get("/v1/ready").json()
    assert _counts() == before
    assert len(calls) == 1  # reads never invoke the model


def test_list_sanitizes_customer_text(client):
    secret = "sk-SECRETVALUE12345678"
    _submit(client, "SANITIZED",
            message=f"help api_key={secret} please")
    listed = client.get("/v1/agent/cases").json()
    match = [i for i in listed["items"] if i["case_id"] == "SANITIZED"]
    assert len(match) == 1
    assert secret not in match[0]["message"]
    assert secret not in json.dumps(listed)


def test_readiness_and_access_basics(client):
    ready = client.get("/v1/ready").json()
    assert ready["ok"] is True and ready["queued_depth"] == 0
    assert ready["oldest_queued_age_s"] is None
    assert "worker" in ready["note"].lower()
    _submit(client, "READY-Q")
    assert client.get("/v1/ready").json()["queued_depth"] == 1
    # Demo faults stay disabled; CORS headers are served for browsers.
    assert client.post("/v1/demo/faults", json={
        "case_id": "X", "run_id": "RUN-1",
        "step": "reserve", "point": "transient"}).status_code == 403
    cors = client.get("/v1/health",
                      headers={"Origin": "http://localhost:3000"})
    assert cors.headers.get("access-control-allow-origin") == \
        "http://localhost:3000"


def test_openapi_covers_new_reads(client):
    paths = client.get("/openapi.json").json()["paths"]
    for route in ("/v1/agent/cases", "/v1/inventory", "/v1/ready",
                  "/v1/agent/cases/{case_id}",
                  "/v1/agent/cases/{case_id}/timeline",
                  "/v1/agent/cases/{case_id}/continue"):
        assert route in paths, route


def test_entrypoint_supervision_with_fake_children():
    import shutil
    import subprocess

    bash = shutil.which("bash")
    if bash is None:  # pragma: no cover - Windows without Git bash
        pytest.skip("bash unavailable; supervision semantics documented "
                    "in docker-entrypoint.sh")
    env = dict(os.environ, SWAPDESK_WORKER_CMD="sleep 300",
               SWAPDESK_API_CMD="exit 3")
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [bash, "docker-entrypoint.sh"], capture_output=True, text=True,
        timeout=60, env=env)
    # First failing child (exit 3) terminates the run: status propagates,
    # and the run ends far sooner than the 300s sleeper (bounded cleanup).
    assert proc.returncode == 3, proc.stderr[-500:]

## Legacy routes (benchmarks only — frontend must not use)

- `POST /v1/tickets` (201, synchronous deterministic policy),
  `GET /v1/cases/{id}`, `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline`,
  `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue`. Unchanged behavior.
- `POST /v1/demo/faults`, `DELETE /v1/demo/faults`: `403` unless
  `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS=1`. Customer execution never depends on
  them.
- `GET /v1/fixtures`, `GET /v1/health`: unchanged, safe for the frontend.

## GET /v1/agent/cases → 200 (inbox list)

Newest first. Read-only: no model calls, no business writes. Each item
uses the same resolver as the detail endpoint (list/detail agree),
including runs without business state. `total` and `summary` cover the
full filtered population, not the page.

Query params: `execution` (one of `queued|running|waiting_input|
completed|failed`), `outcome` (one of `arranged|clarification|denial|
escalation`), `limit` (default 25, max 100), `cursor` (opaque,
from a previous `next_cursor`). Invalid values are `422`.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "case_id": "CASE-9f3a2c1b",
      "message": "Please exchange ITEM-01 on order ORD-1001 for size 42",
      "order_id": "ORD-1001",
      "order_item_id": "ITEM-01",
      "size": "42",
      "qty": 1,
      "execution_status": "completed",
      "outcome": "arranged",
      "current_run_id": "RUN-1",
      "runs": ["RUN-1"],
      "created_at": "2026-10-11T07:00:00+00:00",
      "updated_at": "2026-10-11T07:00:18+00:00",
      "reply": "Exchange arranged: ..."
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null,
  "total": 1,
  "summary": {
    "execution_status": {"completed": 1},
    "outcome": {"arranged": 1}
  }
}
```

`outcome: null` reads as `"pending"` in the outcome summary. The
customer `message` is credential-scrubbed before return.

## GET /v1/inventory → 200 (real stock)

Actual stock keyed by SKU and size, ordered by `(sku, size)`.
`available = on_hand - held`. Only SKU/size/count fields — no
warehouse or product names invented. Pure read: unknown database reads
as empty; nothing is seeded, reserved, released, or reset.

Query params: `sku` / `size` (exact match), `limit` (default 100, max
500), `offset` (default 0).

```json
{
  "items": [
    {"sku": "AIRFLOW-RUNNER", "size": "42",
     "on_hand": 9, "held": 0, "available": 9}
  ],
  "limit": 100,
  "offset": 0,
  "total": 14,
  "read_at": "2026-10-11T07:05:00+00:00"
}
```

## GET /v1/ready → 200 (deployment signal, not proof)

Queue-state readiness for the single-worker SQLite deployment:
`queued_depth`, `oldest_queued_age_s`, `last_terminal_at`. A healthy
`/v1/health` with growing queued depth/age means no worker is draining.
This endpoint cannot prove a worker process is alive.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "service": "swapdesk",
  "queued_depth": 0,
  "oldest_queued_age_s": null,
  "last_terminal_at": "2026-10-11T07:00:18+00:00",
  "note": "queue state only: a growing queued depth or age means no worker is draining, not that one is healthy"
}
```

## Access posture before public paid intake (analysis, no change made)

- CORS is not authentication: it only lets browsers call. Anyone with
  the URL can submit paid agent tickets today.
- Per-run request caps bound generations per run, not aggregate spend:
  there is no rate limiting and no cross-case budget.
- Secrets today: provider/telemetry keys live only as server env vars
  (never in the browser bundle, never in the image: `.env*`, `*.pem`,
  `*.key` excluded from the build context). Keep it that way.
- Demo faults stay disabled unless explicitly enabled.
- Recommended before any public paid intake (not implemented here):
  a verified platform access gate (private service + identity-aware
  proxy) or minimal server-side protection (admin key on `POST`
  routes plus per-IP rate limits). No access was changed in this task,
  and nothing here was deployed.

## Build an agent that works (literally)

**Build an AI agent, or a team of agents, that completes a substantial task from start to finish.** Give it a goal, tools and an environment; let each result guide its next action. All projects compete for the same prizes.

### Focus areas

Planning

Break a goal into actionable steps.

Tool use

Choose tools, supply inputs and handle responses.

State

Retain state across steps, runs and failures.

Context

Bring in relevant information; leave out the rest.

Execution

Keep long tasks running to completion.

Recovery

Handle failures and unexpected results.

Verification

Check that results are correct.

Iteration

Use each result to choose the next step.

See example tasks

These examples show the size of task we have in mind. They aren't separate tracks, and you don't have to build one of them.

-   **Fix a GitHub issue**An agent investigates a GitHub issue, writes and tests a fix, and proposes the fix.
-   **Answer a research question with sources**An agent splits a question into smaller questions and gathers evidence for each one. When sources disagree, the agent works out which source to trust and writes an answer with citations.
-   **Watch a running system**An agent watches a running system for unusual behavior. When the agent finds a problem, it looks for the cause and takes an action to fix it.
-   **Several agents working together**Several worker agents each solve part of a task on their own. A coordinator agent then combines their results and settles any disagreements.
-   **Work while things change**An agent works on a long task while the environment it works in keeps changing.

## FAQs

When and where is neatHack?

neatHack is a 48-hour online hackathon on October 10–12, 2026, starting Saturday at 12:30 PM IST. The kickoff call is at 9:00 AM IST on October 10. Submissions open October 12 at 7:00 PM IST, with a planned close around 11:55 PM IST. The final cutoff will be announced on Discord. Winners are announced on October 16.

Can I build with a team?

Come solo or in a team of 1–4 people. Every member must register on Luma using the same team name, and each person can join only one team.

What can I build beforehand?

You can plan your idea in advance, but all code must be written between the start on October 10 and the deadline on October 12. Finished or half-built projects cannot be brought into the event. Use neatlogs throughout development to capture traces, investigate failures, identify bottlenecks and improve your agent.

How many tracks are there?

There is one track, Build an agent that works (literally), and every project competes for the same prizes. You can build a single agent or a system of several agents. The example tasks are ideas, not separate tracks.

Do I have to use a partner technology?

Yes. Every project must use neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai, with a clear role for each in building the agent or planning its business. Your demo must cover all three tools.

What do I need to submit?

Each team submits one project as a public quote post of the official neatlogs submission post on X before the confirmed cutoff. Use Submit on X to open the draft, fill in your team, name, project, public repository and demo link, keep the official post attached, then publish on X. Include supporting evidence in your repository. Include a demo video of three minutes or less and a public code repository. The video must explicitly cover neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai: architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning and result for each tool. Judges must be able to verify that commits were made during the hackathon. Submissions open October 12 at 7:00 PM IST, with a planned close around 11:55 PM IST. Submit any time during this window; the final cutoff will be announced on Discord. Entries after the confirmed cutoff will not be judged. The Submit on X button appears once the window and official post are live. Opening the draft alone does not submit your project. neatlogs and cfo.ai will engage with the first 50 quote tweets.

How are projects judged?

Mentors score each project using the published criteria. The agent is worth 30% of the final score, the use of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai is worth 25%, and the demo video is worth 20%. Building in public is worth 15%, and usefulness and originality are worth 10%. The judges' decision is final, and the community winner is judged separately.

How does the community winner work?

The community winner goes to the project that generates the strongest genuine community interest during the hackathon. We look at the quality and creativity of the product and demo, the quality of the launch and content, shares and discussion, genuine engagement, and whether people are excited enough to try, share or talk about it. Existing audience size or follower count does not decide the winner. The project must use neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai, but partner usage is not part of community winner scoring. Bought likes or bot activity will disqualify a team.

What are the conduct rules?

Be respectful in Discord and all event spaces. Harassment, spam or plagiarism will result in removal from the hackathon.

Does the AWS allowance cover AI model APIs?

No. Bedrock isn’t included in the hackathon AWS accounts. The $25 allowance per team or solo covers only the approved AWS services. For models, verify the team leader’s check-in email at neatlogs.com/hackathon/models to claim a separate shared LiteLLM key with a $20 budget for Nova and Claude. Your AWS access email includes the permitted services and usage rules.

Where can I get help and credits?

Join neatlogs.com/discord for official neatHack communication. AWS credits go to the first 350 teams to complete web check-in. Fully checked-in teams and solo participants can claim one shared $20 LiteLLM key at neatlogs.com/hackathon/models, while keys are available. Crustdata gives 5,000 credits to everyone participating. Dodo Payments credits are for the top three winners only: $5,000 for first, $3,000 for second and $1,000 for third. Each winner gets 3 months of neatlogs Pro (worth $1500). Access and redemption details will be published with the resources. Workshops and office hours run on both days.

Assessment done, measured against the published requirements (checked live: submissions open **Oct 12, 7:00 PM IST**, close ~11:55 PM IST; judging weights confirmed). Here's where SwapDesk stands:

## How far we've come (by judging weight)

**The agent — 30%: strong.** A real tool-using LangGraph agent that completes exchanges end to end (reserve → return → label → arrange), with idempotency, consent rules, policy enforcement, recovery via operation-status re-query, and DB-derived replies it can't hallucinate. Proven live multiple times (arranged/denial/clarification all observed for real), plus 136 passing deterministic tests. Async queue + worker, inbox list, inventory, readiness reads, Docker/Render blueprint all exist.

**Tools — 25%: mostly strong, one risk.**
- *neatlogs*: deep integration (workflow/tool/model spans, explicit LLM spans added, before/after evidence doc, live traces retrieved). **Risk: their ingest API was erroring today (502/503)** — traces exist but delivery flaked. If judges can't open trace links, this weakens.
- *Entire*: checkpoints linked to every commit, pushes carry refs. Solid.
- *cfo.ai*: business plan + financial model filed in `docs/business/`. Solid.

**Demo video — 20%: not started.** Nothing recorded. Needs ~1:40 agent story + ~1:20 covering all three tools, ≤3 min total.

**Building in public — 15%: weakest.** Zero X posts with #neatHack found. This is 15% of the score sitting empty — cheapest points available (post traces/screenshots as you go).

**Usefulness/originality — 10%: honest but thin.** It solves a real shop problem, but customer support is crowded (the build plan itself concedes originality will score low). Execution evidence is the play here, and it exists.

## What's left (in priority order)

1. **Frontend ↔ backend integration** — dashboard is still mock-only; contract is published, needs Joshua/Chidi to wire it. Without this there's no clickable demo, only curl.
2. **Video** — nothing exists; needs the agent story + all three tools explicitly.
3. **X posts** — none; start now, tag #neatHack, each with a trace or checker result.
4. **Submission mechanics** — submission is a quote-post on X during tomorrow 7:00–11:55 PM IST window; needs team registered on Luma, web check-in done (also unlocks AWS credits + the shared LiteLLM key). Verify check-in status.
5. **Log hygiene** — `hackathon.md`'s Demo/Limitations/Submission sections still say "no backend code yet"; license unchosen.
6. **Spend context** — we've used cents of model calls; note the official shared key stops at **$20**, so live testing has a hard ceiling — fine for our scale, but no room for a big benchmark splurge.
7. **Deferred engineering** (only if time): access gate before any public endpoint, Docker build verification (daemon was down), full 42-run re-baseline.

Bottom line: the build is ~75% of the way there in substance — the remaining work is almost entirely **demo, integration, posting, and submitting**, not backend engineering. The single biggest risk to score is neatlogs delivery being flaky at judging time, followed by the empty building-in-public column.
